name: August 20, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 20, 2024
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 6:35 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The f0110wing persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer; Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne
  Guldimann, and Jake Lingo

  ABSENT: Vice Chair Alicia Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor; and Sebastian Spiroglou,
  Recreation Coordinator

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Vice
  Chair Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recreation Manager Manisco reported the agenda for the meeting was posted on
  August 15, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation on Summer Day Camps bv Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou presented information on summer day camp
  programs.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 20, 2024
  Page 2 of 5

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou stated
  that registration enrollment remained consistent despite the declining number of
  Malibu families.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou stated that
  the participant data was gathered from the 2020 U.S. Census.

  Commissioner Lingo stated his son participated in various summer camps and
  commended staff for their work.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Recreation Manager Manisco stated Joe Sichta had four minutes for public
  comment because Julia Morris surrendered her time.

  Malibu Aquatics Foundation President Joe Sichta stated the Commission should
  review the Request for Qualifications (RFQ) process because he struggled to find
  integrity. He stated the selection committee was familiar with recreational
  swimming not competitive swimming organizations. He stated the evaluation
  criteria favored the Malibu Marlins proposal.

  Sue Murphree stated the Commission failed children who are swimming in Malibu.
  She stated the review process for a swim team organization was not adequately
  reviewed, and the wrong organization was selected. She stated children were
  attending other club teams since the Malibu Marlins did not have an adequate
  program for competitive swimming.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Lingo moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-
  0; Vice Chair Peak absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previouslv Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the July 16, 2024 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in July 2024.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 20, 2024
  Page 3 of 5

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Earth Friendly Management Policy Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly Management
  Policy activities and quarterly report from January to June 2024.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Guldimann thanked Recreation Supervisor Orosz for his hard work
  on the Earth Friendly Management Policy. She stated the progress and program
  implementation was evolving, expanding, and innovative.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that the City
  would not incur costs for the Theodore Payne Foundation seed-storing program and
  the city would have access to the seed collection for habitat restoration.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated eco-
  exempt products could be utilized if the Organic Materials Research Institute
  approved them.

  Commissioner Goldfarb suggested using an aggressive approach to removing non-
  native invasive plants from city properties.

  Commissioner Lingo recused himself from Item 5.B. and left the meeting at 7:07
  p.m.

  Malibu Bluffs Park Baseball Field Modifications
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding a proposal from
  Malibu Little League to modify the Malibu Bluffs Park Pony Baseball Field into a
  multi-use baseball and softball field.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Malibu Little League President John Alfano stated seventy players were in the girls'
  softball program, which was increasing in popularity annually. He stated Malibu
  Little League needed a modified field to accommodate softball games, and the
  League would host home games so families did not have to travel every weekend.
  He stated Malibu Little League would incur the costs for the field modification.

  Marissa Coughlan advocated for youth recreational sports and supported the
  modification of the baseball field.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting

  Page 4 of 5

  Commissioner Guldimann supported the proposal and favored the modification of
  the baseball field to a multi-use field.

  Chair Skophammer stated he initially opposed the idea but supported having a
  space for female athletes to practice and play softball games.

  Commissioner Goldfarb indicated agreement and was in favor of the proposal.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission were in favor of modifying the Pony Baseball fleld
  into a multi-use baseball and softball field.

  Commissioner Lingo returned to the meeting at 7:21 p.m.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Fall Program Registration, the
  Fall Recreation Guide, Department Outreach and Marketing, CineMalibu, Park
  Tales, and Creative Workshops.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided an update on Sunset Hikes, Nature Walks
  and Story Time, and Charmlee Wildemess Park.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the
  removal of mustard plants throughout Charmlee Wilderness Park was a significant
  project that would require funding.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the 2024 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award and Capital Improvement Projects.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Lingo stated he resonated with the public comments regarding the
  RFQ process and agreed that leadership should have been involved in the review
  process.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the City received a bid for the Snack Shack Design, and staff were working on the
  Scope of Work and pricing before presenting it to the Council for approval.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the outcome of the RFQ was concerning and the
  process failed. She stated City Council would make the final decision on the
  outcome. She stated documentation accuracy was critical and could be easily
  verified.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 20, 2024
  Page 5 of 5

  Commissioner Guldimann stated that an outside panel to review the RFQ proposals
  was the only option. She stated that the City Council would recommend the
  Commission review the process if further action was needed. She stated she was
  unhappy with the consultant’s process of collecting data and feedback for the
  Community Lands Outreach Proj ect.

  Chair Skophammer stated he spent approximately one hundred hours in meetings
  and reviewing data related to the swim team. He stated it was understood that an
  outside panel would be involved in the final decision regarding the Request for
  Qualifications. He stated he advocated for the two swim team groups to agree to
  pool space. He stated the Commission approved staff to release the Request for
  Qualifications, and he was comfortable with the selected swim team organization.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco provided the
  aquatic program details. She stated water polo would occur during the fall season,
  and the Malibu Marlins had a three—year contract with the option to extend it for a
  year, up to three additional years,

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated population
  trends were measured by the U.S. Census and the Parks Master Plan. She stated
  Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District could provide a comprehensive
  school population report. She stated trends showed the senior population increasing
  and youth population decreasing.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Skophammer adjoumed the meeting at 7:55 p.m.
